clue.text: Unruly babes of French clerics

indicators.note: unruly babes will not stay in line, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gaggle of badly behaved infants belonging to some French priests.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is a French abbot or cleric, and the plural takes an S.

clue.text: A jolly old fellow in the last war

parts.note: Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
old means aged
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: An elderly cheerful chap who served in the most recent war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective for the old fellow, but it is slang for a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Armageddon is the site of the final battle at the end of the world.

clue.text: Bed reduced-it is unsupported

parts.note: a bed is a base, as in a bed of concrete
reduced means made less

explanation.surface: A bed has been cut down and no longer stands up.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim with no foundation is unsupported by evidence.

clue.text: Wasted talks, possibly, about cooked eel

indicators.note: about means the rearranged talks goes around the other piece
possibly signals that the letters of talks may be arranged another way
cooked eel is eel altered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Conversations about preparing eel were a waste of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' looks like a verb or slang for drunk, but it is the definition: very thin. The anagram of the talking word wraps the cooked fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasted, emaciated body is reduced to skin and bone.

clue.text: Beachcomber hit repeatedly, we hear

definitions.meaning: a beachcomber is an idler loafing along the shore
spoken, the two-word verb sounds like the one-word noun

explanation.surface: A beachcomber is struck again and again, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' marks the second sense as a sound match: the phrasal verb 'lay about' is spelt as two words but heard as the one-word noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer or idler on the shore, and a phrase meaning to lash out at someone on every side.

clue.text: Mislay contents of closet

indicators.note: the contents of the word closet are the letters inside it, without its first and last

explanation.surface: Losing track of the things kept in a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to misplace it so it cannot be found.

clue.text: Regulates new signal

indicators.note: a new version of signal has its letters arranged differently

explanation.surface: A fresh signal controls the traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: To align things is to adjust them into the proper order or position.

clue.text: Goods lost in transport? There is resentment when top of rickshaw is missing

indicators.note: is missing signals that the letter is taken out of the word for resentment

parts.note: outrage is strong anger or resentment

indicators.note: the top of rickshaw is its first letter

explanation.surface: Cargo gets lost and people are furious when a rickshaw loses its roof.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a technical sense of the word: the quantity of goods lost in transit or storage.
explanation.definitionFit: In commerce, outage is the shrinkage or loss of goods while they are shipped or stored.

clue.text: Sound horn both ways

indicators.note: both ways says the word reads the same whether forwards or backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Blowing a horn in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A toot is the short blast a car horn or trumpet makes.

clue.text: Hands put out in error, damsel is in distress

indicators.note: a damsel in distress is upset, so the letters of damsel is are disturbed

explanation.surface: A damsel in distress mistakenly holds out her hands.
explanation.definitionFit: At cards, a hand dealt wrongly is a botched deal, so plural misdeals are cards wrongly given out.

clue.text: He settles abroad with English road-licence

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords
a grant is a licence or permission given

explanation.surface: A man moves overseas with a British driving licence.
explanation.walkthrough: M1 is the main motorway from London north, and the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leaves their country to live in another is an expatriate settler.

clue.text: Where ships are tied up with low loops

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
rings are loops

explanation.surface: A harbour where boats are fastened with short loops of rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth where vessels are secured by ropes, chains or anchors.

clue.text: Ships that carried earliest Greek marbles?

indicators.note: earliest picks the first letter of Greek

parts.note: alleys are large playing marbles, alley being short for alabaster

explanation.surface: Ancient Greek ships that transported marble statues.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is an oared warship of the ancient Mediterranean.

clue.text: RUC's turn-out very small for inspection

indicators.note: a turn-out is a shake-up, so the letters of RUC's are rearranged

parts.note: very small means tiny

explanation.surface: Few police officers from the RUC showed up for the inspection parade.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's former police force; 'turn-out' looks like attendance but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Close examination of something is careful inspection.

clue.text: Landseer's main vantage point?

parts.note: the painter's name is read as one who sees land, and main as the mainmast or sea, so this is a lookout high on a ship

explanation.definitionFit: The lookout platform at the masthead of a sailing ship, from which a sailor spots land.

clue.text: Four-letter words from St Margaret, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that St Margaret produces something unexpected when its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A saint who was shockingly fond of swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is a word of four letters, from the Greek for four and letter.

clue.text: Being brought down to earth in modules, instil order!

indicators.note: order is an imperative telling the solver to put the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to put modules in good order, perhaps after a space mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's illusions is a sobering return to reality.

clue.text: Japanese play on water at lunch time

parts.note: No, or Noh, is classical Japanese drama
taken as written
the tide is the sea's water rising and falling

explanation.surface: A Japanese drama staged on water at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Noontide is midday, the usual hour for lunch.

clue.text: Features of people who look over hilltops?

definitions.text: Features of people who look over hilltops?

parts.words: Features of people who look over hilltops?
parts.note: a brow is the top of a hill, so the facial features above the eyes are playfully seen as eyes surveying hill crests

explanation.definitionFit: The arches of hair above the eyes, sitting on the brow of the face.

clue.text: Ran astern taking part in boat-race? That is restricting!

indicators.note: astern means towards the back, so the word ran is read backwards

parts.note: rowing is what crews do in a boat race

explanation.surface: A crew ran their boat backwards in a race, which held them up.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something narrower limits or confines it.

clue.text: Broadcasts races

definitions.meaning: to relay a programme is to transmit it

explanation.definitionFit: A relay passes a transmission on to listeners, and a relay race passes a baton between team runners.

clue.text: Advantage may be derived from this uncommunicative person

definitions.text: Advantage may be derived from this
definitions.meaning: from the saying that the world is your ..., something to exploit
someone tight-lipped who keeps quiet, shut like a shellfish

explanation.surface: Someone who says nothing may still be useful to exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellfish both yields pearls to profit from and clams up, so it stands for a silent person.

clue.text: Beach hold-all for flood-protection

parts.note: a beach is made of sand
a hold-all is a bag

explanation.surface: A beach bag used to keep rising water out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacks filled with sand are stacked as a barrier against rising floodwater.

clue.text: Bill Sikes' dog shot?

definitions.meaning: the burglar Sikes in Dickens's novel Oliver Twist owns a dog of this name
a shot that strikes the centre of a target

explanation.definitionFit: Sikes's bull terrier in Oliver Twist shares its name with a direct hit on a dartboard or target centre.

clue.text: Well over British border

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A British frontier where the well is overflowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well over' reads as an adverb phrase but is the verb: to brim is to be full to overflowing, as a well might.
explanation.definitionFit: To brim is to be filled to the very top, ready to spill.

clue.text: Give vent to a section of the mitral valve

indicators.note: a section of the words the mitral is a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Releasing pressure through part of a heart valve.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge something, such as a feeling or a sound.

clue.text: Main boat-races in this province of Canada

indicators.note: races suggests the letters of main boat are rushed about into a new order

explanation.surface: Big rowing contests are held in this Canadian province.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is one of the prairie provinces of Canada, with Winnipeg as its capital.

clue.text: Suspicion of corrosion after condensation

indicators.note: after places the corrosion word following the condensation word

parts.note: mist is condensed water vapour
rust is corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: Fearing rust once damp has formed.
explanation.definitionFit: Distrust or doubt about whether someone or something can be relied on.

clue.text: Relieves rents-pound is taken off

indicators.note: is taken off signals that the pound letter is removed from the rents word

parts.note: to rent property is to lease it
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A landlord brings relief by knocking a pound off the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain or worry is to lessen or alleviate it.
